examples: My parents moved to the coast when they retired.
Her parents are very supportive of her career.

trap.en: Parents are only your mother and father. Aunts, uncles, cousins and grandparents are relatives.
trap.es: Parents son solo el padre y la madre. Los parientes en general (tíos, primos, abuelos) son relatives.

items.definition: To have a friendly relationship with someone.
examples: I get on really well with my flatmates.
The two brothers have never got on.

items.definition: To have an argument with someone and stop being friendly with them.
examples: She fell out with her best friend over money.
They fell out years ago and haven't spoken since.

items.definition: To become friends again after an argument.
examples: They had a huge row on Monday, but they'd made up by Wednesday.
It's time you made up with your sister.

items.definition: To end a romantic relationship or marriage.
examples: My neighbours split up last year after ten years together.
He split up with his girlfriend before moving abroad.

items.definition: To respect and admire someone, often because of their achievements or character.
examples: I've always looked up to my older cousin.
Young players look up to him as a role model.

items.definition: To disappoint someone by failing to do what they hoped or expected you would do.
examples: I promised to help him move, and I felt awful when I let him down.
Don't worry, I won't let you down.

items.definition: The family of your husband or wife, especially his or her parents.
examples: We're spending Christmas with my in-laws this year.
She gets on very well with her in-laws.
Only children often form close friendships to make up for having no siblings.
Sibling rivalry can continue well into adult life.

items.definition: Giving help, encouragement or understanding to someone, especially at a difficult time.
examples: My friends were very supportive when I lost my job.
It helps to have a supportive partner.

items.definition: To slowly become less close to someone because you no longer share the same interests or experiences.
examples: We were inseparable at school, but we grew apart after university.
Many couples grow apart without ever having a serious argument.

items.definition: Describing a group of people who know each other well and are very friendly and supportive towards one another.
examples: She grew up in a close-knit community in the Welsh valleys.
The team is small and close-knit, so everyone helps each other.

items.definition: A strong feeling of friendship, love or shared experience that unites people.
examples: There is a special bond between twins.
Working through the crisis together strengthened the bond between them.
collocations: the bond between mother and child

items.definition: Felt or done by two or more people in the same way, or shared by them.
examples: The feeling is mutual: we both think the other is unreasonable.
I met my husband through a mutual friend.

items.definition: Casual talk about other people's private lives, which may not be true or kind.
examples: There's always a lot of gossip in a small office.
I don't want to hear any gossip about my neighbours.
